terms.grammar: pulvis, pulveris m., with fermentārius, fermentāria, fermentārium
terms.comment: Our household word: the powder that does the work of fermentum, leaven (see “leaven”). No reference work has a word for baking powder.

terms.gloss: natron, native soda; in the kitchen, baking soda
terms.comment: Classically natron, the mineral soda of Egypt; its use for baking soda is modern, and ours.

phrases.latin: Paulum pulveris fermentāriī adde, ut placenta intumēscat.
phrases.english: Add a little baking powder, so that the cake rises.

sources: Lewis & Short: pulvis · Lewis & Short: fermentum · Lewis & Short: nitrum
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. soda.
